title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a topos and k a sheaf of rings on X. The data is a monomorphism of k-Modules u: k ↪ I satisfying two conditions:
(a) Ψ = coker u is k-flat.
(b) For all k-modules M, N and all i>0, Γ^i_k(N⊗_k I)⊗_k M is flasque.
Think of I as an acyclic, flasque-type envelope of k, so that Ψ = I/k behaves cohomologically like k[1].

Lemma. For every k-module S there is a 'universal' mono u_S: S ↪ Ñ, meaning it stays a mono after any tensorisation. It satisfies:
(a') if S is flat, coker u_S is flat;
(b') Γ^i(Ñ⊗N)⊗M is flasque for all i>0 and all N, M.
Proof: take Ñ = I⊗_k S and u_S = u⊗id_S. Then (a') follows from (a) and (b') from (b), replacing N by S⊗N.

Definition. 𝒟ℛ^{**}_pd(k,u) = Γ^*_k(Ψ)⊗_k Λ^*_k Ψ.
- This is the divided-power de Rham algebra of the module Ψ, with d(γ_n(x)) = γ_{n-1}(x)·dx.
- It is bigraded: the exponential (weight) degree is n+m on Γ^nΨ⊗Λ^mΨ, and the categorical degree is m. Total degree = exponential + categorical, with sign alternation in the categorical degree.
- It is a commutative differential PD-algebra, with PD structure on the ideal of positive bidegrees.
- Grothendieck calls it a 'réalisation' (or 'résolution'; reading uncertain) of k{T}. Here k{T} is the PD de Rham complex k⟨T⟩⊗Λ(dT) of the PD line, with T of categorical degree 0 and (apparently) total degree 1. Indeed, if Ψ were k·T one would recover exactly k{T}, so the construction is a twisted/derived PD line in which Ψ plays the role of 'k[1]'.
- Then DR_pd(k,u) = Γ(X, 𝒟ℛ_pd(k,u)), a global bigraded alternating PD-dga.

Goal of the page. Make DR_pd(k,u) an invariant of (X,k) alone. Let 𝔻ℝ^{**} be the category of bigraded (degrees ≥0), alternating, differential PD-rings (presumably localized at some class of weak equivalences). The claim is that the DR_pd(k,u), for k fixed and u varying, form a transitive system of isomorphisms in 𝔻ℝ^{**}.

Argument:
1. A morphism λ: I → I' under k induces λ^{**}: DR(u) → DR(u'), which is asserted to be an isomorphism in 𝔻ℝ^{**}.
2. For arbitrary u, u', take the pushout S = I ⊔_k I' and embed S ↪ N by the lemma. This gives DR(u) ≅ DR(N) ≅ DR(u').
3. Independence of the choice of S ↪ N: given two choices N, N', form N'' = N ⊔_S N', embed it by the lemma again, and compare.
4. Transitivity follows by a diagram chase.

This is the standard 'filtered category of choices' argument, as for independence of injective or flasque resolutions. The likely purpose, given the 1976 IHES lecture title, is a canonical strictly (graded-)commutative divided-power dg model attached to cohomology of a ringed topos with arbitrary coefficient ring. That would be a PD analogue, valid in any characteristic, of Sullivan-type commutative cochains, with the nonadditive functors Γ^n applied to a flasque envelope of k.
errors: The key claim that λ^{**} is an isomorphism in 𝔻ℝ^{**} is asserted without proof. It is only plausible if 𝔻ℝ^{**} is a localization, e.g. at quasi-isomorphisms, and if Γ^nΨ⊗Λ^mΨ are Γ(X,-)-acyclic. Hypothesis (b) controls Γ^i(N⊗I)⊗M, not directly Γ^i(Ψ)⊗ΛΨ, so a filtration argument from 0→k→I→Ψ→0 is implicitly needed.
The definition of 𝔻ℝ^{**} is visibly unfinished: several crossed-out attempts mention a structure 'par bidegré (1,0)'. Which morphisms are inverted is never stated.

For the pushout step one needs the composite k → S → Ñ = I⊗S to satisfy (a) and (b). (a) holds because its cokernel is an extension of flat modules (Ψ⊕Ψ', then Ψ⊗S). (b) follows from (b'). These checks are left implicit but are correct.

The meaning of 'résolution/réalisation de k{T}' is not made precise. Since the weight-n pieces of the PD de Rham complex of a flat module are exact for n≥1, the sheaf complex alone resolves only k. The interesting content must come from the bigrading combined with Γ(X,-) of non-acyclic terms, and this is not spelled out on the page.

ideas.what: Choice of a mono k ↪ I with flat cokernel Ψ such that all Γ^i(N⊗I)⊗M are flasque, together with a lemma producing 'universal' (tensor-stable) monos S ↪ I⊗S inheriting these properties.
ideas.modern_name: Acyclic/flasque envelope adapted to a non-additive functor (Γ-acyclic resolutions; cf. Dold–Puppe-style nonadditive derived functors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Puppe (nonadditive derived functors), Illusie (Complexe cotangent, use of Γ, Λ on modules over topoi)

ideas.what: Divided-power de Rham algebra Γ*(Ψ)⊗Λ*(Ψ) of a flat module, bigraded (exponential + categorical degree), with PD structure on the ideal of positive bidegrees; viewed as a twisted/derived realization of the PD de Rham complex k{T} of the PD line.
ideas.modern_name: PD de Rham (Koszul) complex of a module; PD Poincaré lemma
ideas.where_published: Crystalline ideas in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), but not this construction

ideas.what: Global object DR_pd(k,u) = Γ(X, Γ*(Ψ)⊗ΛΨ) proposed as a canonical (choice-independent) commutative bigraded PD-dga attached to a ringed topos (X,k).
ideas.modern_name: Strictly commutative PD/divided-power cochain models; commutative models of cochains in positive characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); positive characteristic: Mandell (E∞ models), Cartan/May (PD and Steenrod structures)

ideas.what: Independence of the choice of envelope via pushouts I ⊔_k I' and N ⊔_S N', giving a transitive system of isomorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Contractible/filtered category of choices; canonical object up to unique isomorphism
ideas.where_published: Same style of argument throughout EGA/SGA (independence of resolutions)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a functorial, choice-independent construction of a commutative bigraded divided-power differential algebra from any ringed topos (X,k). It is built by applying the nonadditive functors Γ^n, Λ^m to a flasque envelope k ↪ I, with Ψ = I/k playing the role of a degree-one variable T. This looks like an attempt at a strictly commutative PD 'cochain algebra' over arbitrary k, a characteristic-free analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms. The defining category 𝔻ℝ^{**} and the precise invariant (what the object 'realizes') are left unfinished.
missed.quote: 𝒟ℛ^{**}_pd(k,u) = Γ*(Ψ)⊗_k ΛΨ Anneau bigradué ... réalisation de k{T} ... système transitif d'isos dans 𝔻ℝ^{**} entre les DR^{**}_pd(k,u), pour k fixé et u variable
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Commutative models of cochains in positive or mixed characteristic are an active theme: E∞ and PD models, derived divided-power algebras, Mandell's theorem, Bhatt–Lurie / Raksit-type derived de Rham with PD. A 1976 Grothendieck proposal producing such an object via nonadditive functors on a flasque envelope would be historically relevant. Whether it actually computes H*(X,k) or yields cohomology operations is unclear from this page alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is mostly a routine independence-of-choices argument. The underlying idea, though, is a canonical bigraded commutative PD-dga attached to an arbitrary ringed topos, built from Γ and Λ of a flasque envelope. It is unpublished and anticipates later interest in commutative/PD cochain models. Its content and aims are too sketchy here to rate higher.
transcription_corrections: Hypothesis (b) reads 'Γ^i(N⊗_k I)⊗M est flasque' (second module is M, not N).
Lemma: '∃ k-mono S ↪ Ñ ... (reste mono par tensorisation), et si S plat ⇒ coker u_S plat' rather than '[?] extension des scalaires'.
'résolution de k{T}' is more likely 'réalisation de k{T}', and the parenthesis reads '(on deg cat T=0, deg tot T=1)' rather than 'deg dT = 1'.
Bigrading phrase: 'Anneau bigradué (degré exponentiel + alterné quand degré cat)', i.e. alternating with respect to the categorical degree.
'Soit 𝔻ℝ^{**} la cat des anneaux bigradués (i deg ≥0) alternés, diff à p.d.' with crossed-out attempts mentioning 'bidegré (1,0)'.
